memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The bull and the goat for the sin offerings, whose blood was brought into the Most Holy Place to make atonement, must be taken outside the camp; their hides, flesh and intestines are to be burned up. The man who burns them must wash his clothes and bathe himself with water; afterward he may come into the camp." - Lev 16:27-28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The blood went in. The bodies went out.

Whatever was left of those animals was carried beyond the boundary of the camp and burned — away from the tents, away from the people, in the place of exclusion.

The writer of Hebrews saw this and could not let it go. The high priest carries the blood of animals into the Most Holy Place as a sin offering, but the bodies are burned outside the camp. And so Jesus also suffered outside the city gate to make the people holy through his own blood (Heb 13:11-12).

Jesus was not killed in the temple. He was not executed in a place of honour. He died on a rubbish hill outside the walls of Jerusalem, between two criminals, in the place reserved for what the city wanted removed.

He went to the place of exclusion so that the excluded could come in.

And then Hebrews turns it into an invitation: Let us, then, go to him outside the camp, bearing the disgrace he bore (Heb 13:13). Following Christ has never been the road to respectability. Sometimes it leads outside — away from approval, into places the comfortable avoid.

He is out there. He always has been.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Has following Christ ever cost you standing or respectability?
2. Where might Jesus be calling you "outside the camp"?
3. What does it mean that He suffered in the place of the excluded?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You suffered outside the gate so that I could be brought in. Give me courage to follow You outside the camp, even where it costs me comfort or approval. Amen.
